# What the release compiles for the tantivy4java native library.
#
# One line per tantivy4java version that pom.xml may name:
#
#   <version> <tantivy4java commit> <quickwit fork commit> <tantivy fork commit>
#
# build-native.sh fetches exactly the tantivy4java commit listed here, and
# refuses to build unless
#   * the tag v<version> in indextables/tantivy4java still points to it, and
#   * the Cargo.lock at that commit resolves indextables/quickwit and
#     indextables/tantivy to the two fork commits listed here.
# A fork column is "-" when that tantivy4java version does not use the fork.
#
# When pom.xml moves to a new tantivy4java version, add a line for it in the
# same pull request (keep the old lines: they are needed to dry-run or
# re-run older tags):
#
#   bash .github/scripts/release/build-native.sh print-pin <version>
#
# print-pin also says, on standard error, whether each fork commit is on the
# fork's default branch, warns when it is only on another branch or tag, and
# refuses when it is on none (such a commit can come from somebody's fork of
# the fork). Review that output and the printed commits before committing
# the line; from then on they are what a release is allowed to build.
